title: Eval-Driven Development: Building the Evals Your Product Needs
summary: How teams build application evals that actually steer development: start from observed failures, turn them into a golden set of the right size, pick the cheapest grader that is trustworthy for each criterion, calibrate model judges, gate releases in CI without drowning in false alarms, and close the loop with online monitoring.
objectives: After this lesson you can run an error-analysis pass on traces and turn the failure taxonomy into binary, testable criteria
Size a golden set for a target margin of error and split it into regression and capability suites
Choose between code assertions, model judges and human review for each criterion, and estimate grading cost
Measure a judge's true-positive and true-negative rates and correct an observed pass rate for judge error
Design a CI eval gate and compute its false-alarm and miss rates, then connect it to online monitoring
prerequisites: Success criteria from [/learn/evaluation/success-criteria](/learn/evaluation/success-criteria), judges and kappa from [/learn/evaluation/llm-as-judge](/learn/evaluation/llm-as-judge), error analysis from [/learn/evaluation/error-analysis](/learn/evaluation/error-analysis), and significance testing from [/learn/evaluation/comparing-systems](/learn/evaluation/comparing-systems).
